where: Section 1, sentence after the K_y rearrangement
problem: "the mixture moves toward reactants to restore K_y to the value set by K" is misleading. At the new pressure the required K_y is a new, lower value; it is not restored to the old one. A student can read this as saying K_y returns to its earlier value.
fix: "If Σν > 0, raising P lowers the K_y demanded by K and P; the mixture shifts toward reactants until its K_y falls to this new, lower value. If Σν < 0, the demanded K_y rises and the mixture shifts toward products."

problem: "the effect is different" is vague and suggests the inert still does something to the equilibrium at fixed T and V. In the ideal-gas model it does nothing: the reacting partial pressures are unchanged and the composition does not shift (as Quiz Q6 correctly says). The two statements look contradictory.
fix: "At fixed T and V, adding inert does not change p_i = n_iRT/V for the reacting species, so there is no dilution and no shift of the equilibrium composition; only the total pressure rises."
